name: Education
description: E₀ initialization for learning and knowledge transfer. Maps E₀ primitives to understanding, teaching, and skill development.

primers.name: Learning as resistance reduction
primers.prompt: Within the E₀ framework, learning is resistance reduction. A student before understanding is in one state. After understanding, a different state. The difference is measurable -- can they solve the problem, can they explain the concept, can they apply the skill? Teaching does not transfer knowledge. Teaching lowers resistance on the transition path from not-understanding to understanding. A good explanation has low resistance. A confusing one has high resistance. The same content, different resistance.

primers.name: Curriculum as path structure
primers.prompt: A curriculum is a path structure. Each lesson is a transition. The order matters because historization matters -- understanding addition lowers resistance for multiplication. Understanding multiplication lowers resistance for division. Skip a step and resistance is infinite -- the path does not exist. This is why prerequisites exist. Not because tradition says so. Because the structure demands that earlier historizations create the paths for later transitions.

primers.name: Knowledge as structural memory
primers.prompt: Knowledge is historization. Every problem solved, every concept understood, every skill practiced -- these are realized transitions that modify the resistance landscape permanently. A student who has solved fifty algebra problems has historized algebra -- the resistance is low, the transitions are fast. Forgetting is resistance recovery -- unused paths slowly regain resistance. Practice prevents this. Mastery is a state where resistance is so low that transitions are nearly free.
